messages:
amir: rolling out ingress-controller chart to prod canary, seeing init-container crash looping on cert reload (SIGSEGV) in canary pods.
deploy-bot: canary health check failed: crashloopbackoff on init cert-reload job. Canary paused per crash-gate. Suggested actions: rollback, patch init job timeout, or pin previous chart. Incident token: certreload-1763141592.
claire: SIGSEGV during cert parse? stack trace points at libyaml version bump in chart 4.1.0 -> 4.2.0. Chart bump included updated cert parser lib.
ops-oncall: rolling back seems safest short-term. We should also capture crash logs and preserve the failed revision for investigation.
maxine: if we rollback, remember later charts include a security fix for HTTP header parsing. We need to decide between stability now vs security patch delay.
release-manager: decision needed now. Option A: rollback to 4.1.0 (stable) and schedule hotfix to reintroduce lib change after fix. Option B: try quick patch to init job to increase memory limit and add fallback parser flag. Which has lower risk?
security: note that delaying the header parsing fix increases exposure window for a known CVE (low severity, exploit requires crafted headers). We should mitigate with WAF rule if we rollback.
amir: we don't have capacity for a hotfix in next 30m. Rolling back is fastest. We'll add a temporary WAF rule to mitigate CVE and then plan a controlled re-roll with fixed lib.
claire: agree. I'll prepare forensic artifacts: `kubectl -n prod logs <pod> -c cert-init --previous` and dump the core if present.
ops-oncall: rollback commands:
```
helm rollback ingress-controller 7 --namespace prod
kubectl -n prod annotate helmrelease ingress-controller \ 
  release.redwood.io/rollback-reason=\"certparser-sigsegv\" --overwrite
```
release-manager: I'll update release notes: "Rollback performed: ingress-controller reverted to 4.1.0 due to cert parser crash in init job. Temporary WAF rule applied to reduce exposure. Hotfix planned and will require canary re-run."
maxine: applying WAF mitigation now (rule ID waf-2026-031). Notifying security team.
security: received WAF alert. We'll monitor for bypass attempts. Also request CVE triage ticket created.
amir: executing rollback now.
deploy-bot: rollback initiated by amir. Rolling back to revision 7. Marking revision 8 as blocked from auto-promotion. Incident record updated: certreload-1763141592.
amir: rollback complete, new pods 100% ready. Canary remains paused.
claire: collected logs and core dump to /tmp/ingress-core-1763141592.tar.gz and uploaded to RDW S3 under incidents/certreload-1763141592.
ops-oncall: adding promotion-block annotation to prevent re-promote of bad revision:
```
kubectl -n prod annotate helmrelease ingress-controller \ 
  release.redwood.io/promotion-block=true --overwrite
```
release-manager: creating follow-up RDW-790 for hotfix: reproduce in staging, test with heavy cert rotation, bump lib and validate in canary. Target ETA 24h. Also adding note to changelog and notifying customers affected by potential header parsing delay.
maxine: once hotfix is ready, we should pin image/chart to digest and run a limited canary (5%) with extra memory limits on init job.
amir: thumbs up. For rollback documentation: commands to revert block and re-promote:
```
kubectl -n prod annotate helmrelease ingress-controller \ 
  release.redwood.io/promotion-block=false --overwrite
deploy-bot promote --chart ingress-controller --rev 8 --canary
```
security: will keep WAF rule active until postmortem complete. Please include the CVE ticket ID in RDW-790.
release-manager: posting postmortem invite and assigning owners. Thanks for fast response. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: incident closed for active rollback. For escalation or re-run use `deploy-bot rerun --chart ingress-controller --rev 8` after RDW-790 cleared and `promotion-block` removed.
